clue.text: One is barely safe from his depredations

definitions.text: One is barely safe from his depredations

parts.words: One is barely safe from his depredations
parts.note: 'barely' suggests scantily clad, but it means that only someone with bare, empty pockets is safe from this kind of thief

explanation.surface: A warning about a predator from whom nobody is quite safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barely' tempts you towards nudity; the safe person is the one with nothing in their pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: A thief who steals from people's pockets threatens anyone carrying valuables, so only the empty-pocketed are safe.

clue.text: Handy thing on a beach in the States

definitions.meaning: the inner surface of the hand

definitions.text: on a beach in the States
definitions.meaning: a tropical tree, and ... Beach is a Florida resort

explanation.surface: Something useful to take to an American seaside resort.
explanation.definitionFit: The inside of the hand is literally a handy thing, and the tree gives its name to Florida's Palm Beach resort.

clue.text: Insect with tail of fish and head of bird

indicators.note: the second piece goes at the end, the first at the start, as a body with head and tail

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
a roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A description of a hybrid creature, part fish and part bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of bird' puts COCK first and 'tail of fish' puts ROACH after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockroach is a scuttling household pest, a kind of beetle-like bug.

clue.text: Upholder of current affairs ?

parts.note: current affairs reads as the news, but here it means electrical current, carried by overhead cables held up on towers

explanation.surface: A defender of news broadcasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current affairs' is news; here 'current' is electricity, held up high by steel towers.
explanation.definitionFit: A steel tower holding up overhead power lines supports electric cables.

clue.text: Man on the make

parts.note: a man on the make is an ambitious schemer, but here man is what is being made, by God

explanation.surface: A description of a social climber or opportunist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the make' is the idiom for self-seeking; read literally, man is the thing made, by God.
explanation.definitionFit: God as maker of mankind is called the maker of the universe.

clue.text: Artists from Chester

indicators.note: the new word is produced out of the letters of the place, rearranged

explanation.surface: Painters who come from a city in north-west England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' looks like origin; it signals that CHESTER is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Printmakers who engrave plates with acid are a kind of artist.

clue.text: It's good for the race, of course

definitions.text: It's good for the race, of course

parts.words: It's good for the race, of course
parts.note: put 'good' in front of the answer and you get the name of a famous English racecourse, so the word is what 'good' needs to become a course for racing

explanation.surface: Someone praising a remedy as beneficial for a horse race, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' reads as 'naturally' but means 'of a racecourse': Goodwood is a racecourse in Sussex, England, made of GOOD plus this word.
explanation.definitionFit: Glorious Goodwood is a Sussex race meeting; adding timber, the material of trees, to 'good' names the course.

clue.text: Animal put into pies in the Midlands

indicators.note: the animal is what you put into the word pies to get the Midlands place; take the pie letters away to find it

parts.note: the Potteries is the pottery-making district of Staffordshire in the English Midlands

explanation.surface: A creature baked into pies somewhere in central England.
explanation.walkthrough: Put the animal into PIES and you get the Potteries, Stoke-on-Trent's pottery district in the English Midlands; removing P and IES from that leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A river-dwelling mammal with webbed feet is an animal.

clue.text: Here the records can easily be broken

indicators.note: breaking records sounds like setting new bests, but here the letters of the words are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A stadium where athletic records are often beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can easily be broken' rearranges THE RECORDS. 'Here' is the definition: a place, Dorchester, county town of Dorset in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorchester is a Dorset town, so it stands for a place, the 'here' in the clue.

clue.text: Direction not given to in-patients, presumably

definitions.text: Direction not given to in-patients, presumably

parts.words: Direction not given to in-patients, presumably
parts.note: in-patients stay in hospital wards, so they are presumably not sent out of the wards

explanation.surface: Instructions withheld from those staying in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as out wards: in-patients are kept in the wards, not directed out of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Heading away from the centre or towards the outside is a direction.

clue.text: Where one might reasonably expect to get near-beer ?

definitions.text: Where one might reasonably expect to get near-beer

parts.words: Where one might reasonably expect to get near-beer
parts.note: near-beer is a weak low-alcohol drink, but here it is read as beer that is near at hand, as at the pub round the corner

explanation.surface: Wondering where a weak, alcohol-free beer could be bought.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the local' is your neighbourhood pub; 'near-beer' (a weak drink) becomes beer close by.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for the neighbourhood pub, the nearest place to buy a pint.

clue.text: It is meet to do this

definitions.text: It is meet to do this

parts.words: It is meet to do this
parts.note: 'meet' reads as the old adjective meaning fitting or proper, but it is the verb: to meet someone is to come across them

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned pronouncement that some act is fitting and right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meet' sounds like archaic prayer-book language for 'proper'; it is simply the verb for coming face to face.
explanation.definitionFit: To come upon someone unexpectedly is to meet them, the same act the verb names.

clue.text: But she might still suffer from lightheadedness

definitions.text: But she might still suffer from lightheadedness

parts.words: But she might still suffer from lightheadedness
parts.note: lightheadedness reads as dizziness, but a fair-haired woman literally has a light head; this woman has dark hair yet could still feel dizzy

explanation.surface: A remark that even a certain woman could feel faint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lightheadedness' suggests giddiness; split it as light-headed, blonde, which this dark-haired woman is not.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman with dark brown hair is the opposite of a blonde, the 'light-headed' one.

clue.text: Value of a pet in Sussex

definitions.text: Value of a pet in Sussex

parts.words: Value of a pet in Sussex
parts.note: reads as the price of an animal, but the word for value is also the name of a village in West Sussex

explanation.surface: A question about what an animal kept in Sussex would fetch.
explanation.walkthrough: Worth is a village near Crawley in West Sussex, a county in southern England, so the word means both value and a Sussex place.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing's value is what it is worth, and Worth is also a West Sussex village.

clue.text: A beast most given to craft

indicators.note: the letters of the words are handed over to be remade into the vessels

explanation.surface: An animal that loves crafts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given to' looks like 'fond of' but signals that A BEAST MOST is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Vessels propelled by steam engines are boats, and boats are craft.

clue.text: He'll catch it !

parts.note: reads as a threat that someone will be punished, but it means a man who catches animals

explanation.surface: Someone warning that a naughty boy is in for a telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catch it' is the idiom for being punished; here it is literal: a hunter who catches animals in snares.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunter who sets snares to catch animals for their fur.

clue.text: Firing of kitchen ranges ?

parts.note: firing a kitchen range means lighting a stove, but read as gunfire at ranges it means random shots, and stoves heat pots

explanation.surface: Lighting up the stoves in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ranges' suggests stoves; read as shooting, random shots at targets, and split as POTS HOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Random, casual shots at a target, and also pots heated on a stove.

clue.text: Underwriters are not necessarily inferior ones

definitions.text: Underwriters are not necessarily inferior ones

parts.words: Underwriters are not necessarily inferior ones
parts.note: underwriters are insurers, but split as under-writers they are lesser writers; copyists hold a humble rank among writers

explanation.surface: An observation about insurance professionals' standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underwriters' means insurers; read as 'under-writers', writers of lower rank, which copyists need not be.
explanation.definitionFit: Copyists and clerks who wrote documents by hand before printing.

clue.text: Club wear ?

parts.note: club reads as a society or nightclub's dress code, but clubs is a card suit coloured black

explanation.surface: A query about what to wear to a club.
explanation.walkthrough: Clubs is one of the two black suits in a deck of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Clubs and spades are dark-coloured suits in cards; a dark suit is also formal dress.

clue.text: A she-cat makes a faithful companion

indicators.note: the letters of the words before are rearranged, and 'makes' says they form the new word

explanation.surface: A claim that a female cat is the most loyal of friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' rearranges A SHE-CAT. Achates is the loyal friend of Aeneas in Virgil's Aeneid.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Aeneid, Achates is Aeneas's loyal friend, so his name became a byword for a devoted friend.

clue.text: No night-watch, this

parts.note: a night-watch is a guard after dark, but here a watch is a timepiece, and this one only works by daylight

explanation.surface: Someone saying a guard duty is not at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'night-watch' suggests a sentry; read 'watch' as a timepiece, one that needs the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A shadow-casting garden timepiece tells the time only in daylight.

clue.text: Father's wise to go this way

parts.note: father is pa, and the possessive gives PA'S
a sage is a wise person, used here as the adjective

explanation.surface: Advice to follow a parent's prudent path.
explanation.definitionFit: A corridor or route through which you go is a way.

clue.text: This horse was some flier !

parts.note: 'some flier' praises a fast racehorse, but this horse literally flew, having wings

explanation.surface: Praise for a racehorse's speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flier' suggests a fast runner; the winged horse of Greek myth truly flew.
explanation.definitionFit: The winged horse of Greek myth, ridden by Bellerophon.

clue.text: Set seen in a pub at Christmas

indicators.note: the letters are visible inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Something spotted in a bar during the festive season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' says the answer lies inside 'puB AT CHristmas'.
explanation.definitionFit: A group or lot of things made together, such as a set of cakes.

clue.text: Gardeners don't use it to train their runners

definitions.text: Gardeners don't use it to train their runners

parts.words: Gardeners don't use it to train their runners
parts.note: runner beans are trained up canes; athletes, the other runners, are trained on a running circuit

explanation.surface: Gardeners describing how they grow runner beans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runners' are runner beans, climbing plants; athletes train on a running circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Athletes train on an oval running circuit, which gardeners have no use for.

clue.text: Ask again for port

indicators.note: the words before are reworked to produce the place, 'for' saying they stand for it once rearranged

explanation.surface: A request to repeat a question about a fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is the only signal: ASK AGAIN rearranged gives the Japanese port. 'port' may suggest the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Nagasaki is a harbour city on Kyushu in Japan.

clue.text: A meeting of "pushing" young men

parts.note: pushing young men sounds like ambitious youths, but in rugby the forwards literally push in this formation

explanation.surface: A gathering of thrusting, ambitious youths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pushing' means pushy in the surface; in rugby the forwards bind and shove against each other.
explanation.definitionFit: A rugby set piece where the forwards of both sides bind together and push.

clue.text: Where, in short, County types are prone to settle ?

definitions.text: Where, in short, County types are prone to settle

parts.words: Where, in short, County types are prone to settle
parts.note: 'in short' signals the abbreviation of Bedfordshire, an English county, and being prone means lying down, which people do in sleeping furniture

explanation.surface: Asking where upper-class country folk like to make their homes.
explanation.walkthrough: Beds is the short form of Bedfordshire, a county north of London; 'prone' means lying flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for Bedfordshire, and also the furniture people lie on.

clue.text: Places where work's something of a shambles

definitions.text: Places where work's something of a shambles

parts.words: Places where work's something of a shambles
parts.note: a shambles reads as a mess, but its old sense is a meat market or slaughterhouse

explanation.surface: A complaint about chaotic workplaces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shambles' originally meant a slaughterhouse or meat market, as in York's street The Shambles.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaughterhouses, the original sense of a shambles, are where animals are killed for meat.

clue.text: It's way out among the Sappers

indicators.note: one word is placed amid the letters standing for the military group

parts.note: sappers are army engineers, the Royal Engineers, abbreviated RE
taken as written

explanation.surface: An escape route found among army engineers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' puts OUT inside RE, the Royal Engineers, nicknamed the Sappers in the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: A road or course followed to get somewhere is a way.

clue.text: Clovis's chronicler from 24

indicators.note: the answer is taken out of the letters of the solution to clue 24

parts.note: the answer to 24 across, the Japanese port

explanation.surface: A writer who recorded a Frankish king's deeds, hailing from a port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes the last four letters of 24's answer. Saki (H. H. Munro) wrote The Chronicles of Clovis; Clovis was also a Frankish king.
explanation.definitionFit: Saki, pen name of H. H. Munro, wrote the story collection The Chronicles of Clovis.

clue.text: But these students need not be on the same social plane

definitions.text: But these students need not be on the same social plane

parts.words: But these students need not be on the same social plane
parts.note: students taught together share a class at school, though they need not share a social class

explanation.surface: A comment that pupils mixing together may come from different backgrounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'class' has two senses: a school form and a social rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils taught in the same form at school are fellow pupils of that form.
